_note: Every value is extracted from a claim quote by compute.py, or derived from extracted values by a rule stated beside it.

lane_miles.basis: miles between the Dallas-Fort Worth and Houston areas along I-45, the company's figure for the driver-out leg

ikea_route_miles.basis: miles of IKEA's Baytown to Frisco route the leg is part of

arm_feb.basis: readiness measure as of February 2026, percent

arm_jul.basis: readiness measure as of July 2026, percent

arm_aug.basis: readiness measure at the end of August 2026, percent of the safety case's claims and evidence materially complete

arm_target.basis: the readiness measure the company expects to reach before launch, percent

arm_open.basis: percentage points of the safety case's claims and evidence not yet materially complete at the end of August, by the company's own measure

ikea_loads.basis: loads delivered for IKEA over four years, more than

ikea_miles.basis: miles autonomously carrying IKEA goods with a safety observer aboard, more than

autonomous_miles_m.basis: millions of autonomous miles the company has driven since 2019, more than

route_since.basis: year the company began hauling Dallas to Houston with safety drivers

atlas_trucks.basis: driverless trucks owned and operated by Atlas in the Permian as of June 30th, 2026

atlas_hours.basis: cumulative hours of paid driverless operation in the Permian, more than

enforce_days.basis: days after the final rules took effect that TxDMV authorization became enforceable

leg_share_of_route.basis: fraction of IKEA's route the driver-out leg covers, for drawing the leg as a length along the route at one scale; never printed

days_to_year_end.basis: days from the run date to December 31st, the last day of the year the company names for its launch

arm_series.basis: the readiness measure by month of 2026, month number and percent, for drawing as rendered heights at one scale; the month numbers come from the quote's month names
